subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Probability — Cards, Coins, Dice and Balls (W13 B1)

questions.stem: From a standard deck of 52 playing cards, one card is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is the King of Hearts?
questions.explanation: C is correct. There is exactly ONE King of Hearts in a 52-card deck. P = favourable/total = 1/52. Trap: 1/13 = probability of any King (4 Kings in 52 cards = 4/52=1/13); 1/26 = probability of any red King (2 red kings out of 52=2/52=1/26); 4/52 = probability of any King.

questions.stem: A card is drawn at random from a pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a red card?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Red cards = Hearts (13) + Diamonds (13) = 26. P(red) = 26/52 = 1/2. Exactly half the deck is red (hearts and diamonds) and half is black (clubs and spades). Trap: 1/4 = P(hearts only); 3/4 = wrong (complements must add to 1: P(red)=1/2, P(black)=1/2).

questions.stem: Three unbiased coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting all three heads?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Total outcomes for 3 coins = 2³ = 8: {HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT}. Favourable (all heads) = only HHH = 1 outcome. P = 1/8. Alternatively: P(H)×P(H)×P(H) = (1/2)³ = 1/8 ✓. Trap: 1/4 = P(exactly 2 heads); 1/2 = P(more heads than tails for 2 coins, not 3).

questions.stem: Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of numbers on the two dice is 7?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Total outcomes = 36. Pairs summing to 7: (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1) = 6 outcomes. P = 6/36 = 1/6. Note: 7 is the MOST LIKELY sum from two dice. Trap: 7/36 = common mistake thinking '7 outcomes' (there are 6, not 7); 5/36 = sum=8 outcomes (there are 5 pairs summing to 8).

questions.stem: A bag contains 5 red and 3 blue balls. If one ball is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is blue?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Total balls = 5+3 = 8. Blue balls = 3. P(blue) = 3/8. Trap: 5/8 = P(red) not P(blue); 3/5 = blue/(red only) — divides by red count instead of total; 1/3 = blue/(total-blue)=3/5 or some other wrong calculation.

questions.stem: A card is drawn from a pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a face card (Jack, Queen or King)?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Face cards: Jack, Queen, King — 3 types × 4 suits = 12 cards. P = 12/52 = 3/13. Trap: 1/13 = probability of each type separately (e.g., all Jacks = 4/52=1/13); 3/52 = counts only 3 cards (one per type, not all 12); 1/4 = probability if exactly 13 of 52 were face cards.

questions.stem: Two dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is MORE THAN 9?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Sums greater than 9 (i.e., 10, 11, 12): Sum=10: (4,6),(5,5),(6,4)=3; Sum=11: (5,6),(6,5)=2; Sum=12: (6,6)=1. Total=6. P=6/36=1/6. Trap: 5/36 = sums equal to 8 or some other count; 7/36 = often guessed by adding 7 'big sums'; 1/4 = overestimate.

questions.stem: A bag has 4 white and 6 black balls. Two balls are drawn WITHOUT replacement. What is the probability that both are the same colour?
questions.explanation: A is correct. P(both white) = (4/10)×(3/9)=12/90=2/15. P(both black) = (6/10)×(5/9)=30/90=1/3. P(same colour) = 2/15+1/3=2/15+5/15=7/15. Verify: total outcomes=C(10,2)=45; same-colour: C(4,2)+C(6,2)=6+15=21; P=21/45=7/15 ✓. Trap: 8/15 = P(different colours)=1−7/15=8/15 (the complement, not what's asked).

questions.stem: Three coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting AT LEAST 2 heads?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Total outcomes=8. At least 2 heads: exactly 2 heads = {HHT,HTH,THH}=3; exactly 3 heads = {HHH}=1. Total favourable=4. P=4/8=1/2. Shortcut: by symmetry, P(at least 2 heads)=P(at least 2 tails) and P(≥2H)+P(≥2T)=P(≥2H)+P(≥2H) [symmetry] ... actually P(exactly 2H)=P(exactly 2T)=3/8 and P(3H)=P(3T)=1/8. P(at least 2H)=3/8+1/8=4/8=1/2 ✓. Trap: 3/8 = exactly 2 heads (not at least 2); 5/8 = at least 1 head (broader condition).

questions.stem: Two cards are drawn at random from a pack of 52. What is the probability that one is an ace and the other is a king?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Total ways to draw 2 cards = C(52,2)=1326. Favourable (1 ace AND 1 king): C(4,1)×C(4,1)=4×4=16. P=16/1326=8/663. Verify: 16/1326=8/663 ✓ (divide by 2). Trap: 16/663 = not simplified (or forgot to divide C(52,2) = 1326, not 663); 4/663 = counts only 4 combinations (wrong); 1/52 = probability of drawing one specific card.
